transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
I’m here because I feel completely drained. Even walking from my car to the clinic took everything I had, and opening the EHR at work feels like too much.
How long have you been feeling this drained—days, weeks, or longer?
It’s been longer than just a few days. I’ve felt really drained—like even getting from the car to work or opening the EHR takes everything I have.
Over these past weeks, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I’ve mostly just noticed how exhausted I am.
Do you feel rested when you wake up in the morning, or do you still feel tired even after a full night's sleep?
I still wake up tired. My body just feels completely drained, like even getting from the car to the clinic takes everything I have.
Has anyone told you that you snore loudly or stop breathing at times while you're asleep?
I’m not sure. No one’s mentioned that to me, as far as I know.
Have you noticed any unintentional weight gain or weight loss over the past few weeks or months?
Yeah, I think I’ve lost some weight. I barely wanted food and would skip lunch and dinner, then notice my scrubs were hanging looser. Mostly I was just drinking coffee or water.
Have you noticed any unusual bruising, bleeding gums, blood in your stool, or looking unusually pale lately?
I haven’t noticed any of that, no.
Over these past weeks, have you been feeling sad, down, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?
Yeah. After all that energy dropped, I started feeling empty and hopeless most days. Like I’d already ruined my future in healthcare before it even really started.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks or months of feeling this drained, hopeless, or uninterested in things—prior to this current episode?
Yeah. It’s been about nine months now, since I crashed after that high-energy period. I’ve felt depressed, guilty, and exhausted for most of that time.
Can you tell me more about that high-energy period before you crashed—did you notice needing much less sleep, feeling unusually confident, or having racing thoughts during that time?

Yeah. For a while I was only sleeping two or three hours and still felt wired. Lately it’s the opposite—I either wake up before dawn feeling sick with worry, or I sleep half the day and still feel exhausted.
During that high-energy period when you were sleeping only 2-3 hours, did you also feel unusually happy, irritable, or overly confident, and were you much more active or talkative than usual?
Yeah. Some days I felt amazing, like I was unstoppable. But if anyone corrected my documentation or told me to slow down, I’d snap at them like they were insulting me.
Have you noticed any night sweats, persistent fevers, or swollen lumps in your neck, armpits, or groin over these past months?
No, I haven’t noticed any of those.
Have you noticed feeling lightheaded, dizzy, or short of breath when you exert yourself, like when walking or climbing stairs?
I’m not really sure—I haven’t paid much attention to that.
During this depressive period, have you experienced anything unusual, like hearing voices or sounds others don't hear, or having thoughts or beliefs that others say aren't true?
Yeah. During shifts, I’d hear my name over the clinic speaker, or a monitor beeping like it was for me, but nobody else heard it. I’d go looking for a patient who wasn’t actually calling.
